posts.title: How to Tell If a Promo Code Will Work Before You Use It
posts.excerpt: Five quick checks that save you from dead codes, hidden exclusions and surprise renewal prices.
posts.author: Biorals Team
posts.seoTitle: How to Tell If a Promo Code Will Work (5 Quick Checks)
posts.seoDescription: Learn five quick checks to spot expired, restricted or misleading promo codes before you reach checkout and waste your time.
posts.body:
A code that fails at checkout wastes your time and can nudge you into paying full price. These five checks take under a minute.

## 1. Look for a recent check date
A code with no date is a guess. Prefer listings that say when they were last tested and drop anything older than a few weeks for fast-moving retailers.

## 2. Read the exclusions
Most percentage codes exclude sale items, gift cards or certain brands. If your basket is mostly excluded items, the code will not apply.

## 3. Check the minimum spend
A code that needs a high basket total may push you to buy more than you planned. Work out whether the saving is still worth it.

## 4. Confirm region and account rules
Many codes work only in one country or only for new customers. A US-only code will be rejected if you shop from the UK.

## 5. Look at the renewal price
For subscriptions, the first-term discount is often the headline. Note what the service charges after that period before you enter payment details.

If a code still fails, clear the basket, re-enter it exactly as shown and make sure you are signed in to the right account.

posts.title: The Best Time to Buy Almost Anything: A Sales Calendar
posts.excerpt: A month-by-month guide to when TVs, mattresses, fashion and flights are cheapest.
posts.author: Biorals Team
posts.seoTitle: Best Time to Buy: A Month-by-Month Sales Calendar
posts.seoDescription: Use this month-by-month sales calendar to time big purchases like TVs, mattresses, fashion and flights for the lowest prices.
posts.body:
Retailers follow predictable sale patterns. Time your purchase around them and you can save without chasing every coupon.

## January
New-year clearance and white-goods sales. Retailers reset stock, so sofas, bedding and winter clothing drop sharply.

## Spring
Garden and DIY events, plus Easter promotions on food and travel. Book summer flights early.

## Summer
Mid-season fashion sales and Prime Day style events. Electronics and outdoor gear see good knock-downs.

## Black Friday and Cyber Monday
The biggest tech, gaming and appliance discounts. Compare against pre-sale prices to avoid inflated discounts.

## December
Gift sets and partywear peak early, then drop right after Christmas into Boxing Day sales.

## Rule of thumb
Buy out of season where you can. A winter coat is cheapest in spring, and a summer fan is cheapest in autumn.

posts.title: How to Stack Coupons, Cashback and Loyalty Points
posts.excerpt: Layer multiple savings methods legally without breaking a store rules.
posts.author: Biorals Team
posts.seoTitle: How to Stack Coupons, Cashback and Loyalty Legally
posts.seoDescription: Learn how to combine discount codes, cashback and loyalty points in the right order to save the most, without breaking store terms.
posts.body:
Stacking savings is about order and the rules. Do it right and a single purchase can be cheaper by more than one discount.

## Start with the price
Buy at the lowest base price first. A code on an inflated price is not a saving.

## Apply the code, then loyalty
Enter the promo code at checkout, then collect loyalty points on the amount you actually pay.

## Add cashback last
Click through a cashback site after you have your basket ready. It tracks the final paid amount, so resolve codes first.

## Know the limits
Many stores exclude cashback on orders paid partly with gift cards, or void cashback if you use a third-party code. Read each program rules.

## Keep records
Screenshot the code and the confirmed order total. If cashback fails to track, you have the evidence to claim it.

posts.body:
Student discounts are often bigger than public promo codes and available all year. Verifying once unlocks most of them.

## Verify once
Services like a student ID card or an online verification tool confirm your status to many retailers at once.

## Tech and software
Apple, Microsoft and Adobe run education stores. Laptops and creative software are frequently the biggest wins.

## Fashion and sportswear
Many high-street and sportswear brands offer 10 to 15 percent off for students, often stackable with sale prices.

## Food and travel
Delivery apps and railcards give steady student rates that add up over a term.

## Read the rules
Most student codes exclude other promotions and cannot be combined with cashback. Check before you rely on a stack.

posts.title: Black Friday 2026: How to Prepare and Avoid Fake Deals
posts.excerpt: A practical checklist to spot inflated discounts and buy only what you actually need.
posts.author: Biorals Team
posts.seoTitle: Black Friday 2026: Prepare and Avoid Fake Deals
posts.seoDescription: Get ready for Black Friday 2026 with a checklist to track prices, spot inflated discounts and buy only genuine bargains.
posts.body:
Black Friday rewards preparation more than impulse. A little work now means you recognise a real deal when you see one.

## Build a shortlist now
Write down the exact models you want. Vague wishes invite impulse buys.

## Record today prices
Note current prices in a spreadsheet. On the day, compare against your notes, not the slashed sticker price.

## Watch for inflate-then-discount
Some retailers raise prices weeks before the event. Price-history tools expose this quickly.

## Set a hard budget
Decide the total you will spend and stick to it. Bundles and add-ons are where budgets break.

## Check delivery and returns
A great price is no good if delivery arrives after the date you need it, or returns are excluded.

posts.title: Cyber Monday vs Black Friday: Which Has Better Deals?
posts.excerpt: Where each event wins, and how to shop both without overpaying.
posts.author: Biorals Team
posts.seoTitle: Cyber Monday vs Black Friday: Which Is Better?
posts.seoDescription: Compare Cyber Monday and Black Friday to see which has better deals on tech, fashion and home, and how to shop both smartly.
posts.body:
The two biggest online shopping days overlap in stock but differ in focus. Knowing the split helps you wait for the right moment.

## Black Friday strengths
In-store doorbusters, big-ticket electronics and appliances. Inventory is deepest, but the best prices are often limited stock.

## Cyber Monday strengths
Online-only offers, software, small electronics and fashion. Retailers extend weekend deals and add fresh online codes.

## Where they overlap
Most tech and home deals run across the whole weekend, so you do not have to buy on a single day.

## Strategy
Shortlist early, track prices through both days, and buy when the price hits your target rather than guessing which day wins.

## Do not forget returns
Extended holiday return windows often apply, but confirm the dates for anything bought as a gift.

posts.title: How Cashback Sites Really Work (And When They Beat Coupons)
posts.excerpt: Understand tracking, payout windows and why cashback sometimes fails.
posts.author: Biorals Team
posts.seoTitle: How Cashback Sites Work and When They Beat Coupons
posts.seoDescription: Understand how cashback sites track purchases, when they pay out and why cashback sometimes fails, so you can use them with confidence.
posts.body:
Cashback returns a slice of your spend, but the mechanics matter if you want it to actually arrive.

## How tracking works
You click through the cashback site to the retailer. A tracking cookie records the order, and the retailer confirms it later.

## Why it fails
Ad blockers, coupon extensions, paying with a gift card or returning items can void cashback. Start clean and avoid other codes unless allowed.

## When payout arrives
Most sites wait until the retailer confirms and the return window closes. Expect weeks, not days.

## Cashback vs coupon
A coupon gives an instant discount; cashback arrives later. When both are allowed, using the coupon first and cashback second usually saves most.

## Track your claims
Keep order confirmations so you can chase missing cashback before the claim window closes.

posts.title: Free Delivery Codes: How to Never Pay for Shipping Again
posts.excerpt: Thresholds, memberships and codes that wipe out delivery fees.
posts.author: Biorals Team
posts.seoTitle: Free Delivery Codes: How to Avoid Shipping Fees
posts.seoDescription: Learn how free delivery codes, spending thresholds and memberships work so you can stop paying for shipping on online orders.
posts.body:
Delivery fees quietly erode a discount. A few habits keep shipping free.

## Know the threshold
Many stores ship free over a set basket total. If you are close, add a genuinely useful item rather than paying delivery.

## Look for delivery codes
Retailers often release free-delivery codes around sales. These stack well because they do not usually reduce the item price.

## Consider memberships
If you order often, a delivery membership can pay for itself over a year. Do the maths on your order frequency.

## Collect in store
Click and Collect is often free and faster than waiting for a courier.

## Watch the small print
Bulky items, islands and next-day slots are often excluded from free delivery. Check before you rely on it.

posts.title: How to Spot a Fake Discount (and Price-Anchoring Tricks)
posts.excerpt: The psychology retailers use to make a price look lower than it is.
posts.author: Biorals Team
posts.seoTitle: How to Spot a Fake Discount and Price Anchoring
posts.seoDescription: Discover the price-anchoring and fake-discount tricks retailers use, and learn simple checks to confirm a deal is genuinely good.
posts.body:
A crossed-out price is a claim, not a fact. These tricks are common and easy to see once you know them.

## Inflate-then-discount
Some stores raise prices before a sale so the discount looks bigger. Price history exposes it in seconds.

## The anchor price
Showing a high original price makes the sale price feel like a bargain, even when the item is rarely sold at full price.

## Bundle padding
Free extras can hide a higher base price. Compare the item alone across retailers.

## Countdown pressure
Timers and low-stock flags push quick decisions. Step away and check the price elsewhere.

## The simple test
Ask what you would pay elsewhere today. If the answer is similar, the discount is cosmetic.

posts.title: Do Coupon Codes Actually Work on Sale Items?
posts.excerpt: Why most codes exclude sale stock, and how to find ones that do not.
posts.author: Biorals Team
posts.seoTitle: Do Coupon Codes Work on Sale Items? What to Know
posts.seoDescription: Find out whether promo codes work on sale items, why many exclude clearance stock, and how to find codes that do stack with reductions.
posts.body:
One of the most common checkout frustrations is a code that will not apply to discounted items. Here is why, and what to do.

## Why codes exclude sale items
Retailers protect margins on already-reduced stock, so terms often exclude clearance categories.

## Where codes do stack
Some stores allow codes on full-price items plus free delivery on everything. Read the terms line to see what is included.

## Try a different code
If a percentage code fails on sale items, a free-delivery or spend-and-save code may still work.

## Watch the basket order
Sometimes applying a code before adding an item makes it stick. Re-add items in a different order if a code misbehaves.

## When to skip it
If the sale price is already the lowest you have seen, a failing code is not a reason to wait.

posts.title: Newsletter-Only Discount Codes: How to Get Them Fast
posts.excerpt: The signup codes most shoppers never see, and how to use them well.
posts.author: Biorals Team
posts.seoTitle: Newsletter-Only Discount Codes: How to Get Them
posts.seoDescription: Discover how to find newsletter-only discount codes, what welcome offers usually include and how to use them without cluttering your inbox.
posts.body:
Many of the best first-order codes are sent only to email subscribers. A few habits get you there quickly.

## The welcome code
Most stores email a first-order discount within minutes of signup. Use a separate email address to keep your main inbox clean.

## Pop-ups and exit offers
Stores often show a signup prompt as you leave. These frequently contain the highest first-order discounts.

## Use them once, wisely
Welcome codes usually apply to one order, so plan a larger basket rather than a small test purchase.

## Unsubscribe after
You can opt out once you have the code and still use it, unless the terms say otherwise.

## Watch the expiry
Many welcome codes expire within a week or two. Check the date before you save it for later.

posts.title: Abandoned Cart Emails: How to Trigger a Discount
posts.excerpt: A gentle way to nudge a better price on something you nearly bought.
posts.author: Biorals Team
posts.seoTitle: Abandoned Cart Emails: How to Trigger a Discount
posts.seoDescription: Learn how abandoned cart emails work and how to use them politely to unlock a discount code on items you nearly bought.
posts.body:
Retailers would rather recover a near-sale than lose it, and many send a code to win you back. Use this with restraint.

## How it works
Add items, sign in if you have an account, reach checkout and stop before paying. Many stores follow up with a reminder, sometimes with a code.

## Give it a day
Codes usually arrive within 24 to 48 hours. Wait before buying at full price.

## Do not abuse it
Repeatedly abandoning carts can get you flagged. Use it occasionally on genuine purchases.

## Compare the offer
An abandoned-cart code may be smaller than a welcome code. Check which is larger before you choose.

## Finish the purchase
If no code arrives, decide whether the item is worth full price. Do not let the tactic talk you into a purchase.

posts.title: Browser Extensions That Find Working Codes (Safely)
posts.excerpt: How coupon extensions work, what they track and when to disable them.
posts.author: Biorals Team
posts.seoTitle: Coupon Browser Extensions: How They Work and Stay Safe
posts.seoDescription: Understand how coupon browser extensions find codes, what browsing data they can access and how to use them safely at checkout.
posts.body:
Coupon extensions test codes automatically at checkout. They can save time, but understand the trade-offs.

## How they test codes
The extension tries a list of codes in the promo box and keeps whichever reduces the total.

## The privacy trade-off
Many extensions can read the pages you visit. Check permissions and reviews, and remove ones you no longer use.

## Conflicts with cashback
Some extensions interfere with cashback tracking. Disable the extension before clicking through a cashback site.

## Verify the discount
Confirm the applied code actually lowered the price rather than triggering a different offer.

## Best practice
Keep one trusted extension, review its permissions and turn it off for sensitive sites.

posts.title: Price Tracking Tools: Buy at the Real Lowest Price
posts.excerpt: Set alerts and watch history so you buy on the dip, not the spike.
posts.author: Biorals Team
posts.seoTitle: Price Tracking Tools: Buy at the Real Lowest Price
posts.seoDescription: Use price tracking tools and alerts to see a product price history and buy at the genuine lowest price instead of a fake discount.
posts.body:
Price trackers turn guesswork into data. They show what an item really sells for over time.

## See the history
A price-history chart shows the usual selling price and the genuine lows. A sale that sits above the usual price is not a bargain.

## Set alerts
Add the products you want and get an email when the price drops below your target.

## Time the sales
Trackers reveal when a store usually discounts, so you know whether to buy now or wait.

## Combine with codes
Track price and codes together. The best moment is often a genuine low plus a working code.

## Do not over-wait
If an item is already at its historical low and you need it, waiting for a few percent more can backfire.

posts.title: Boxing Day and January Sales: A Shoppers Guide
posts.excerpt: Where the deepest post-Christmas discounts really are.
posts.author: Biorals Team
posts.seoTitle: Boxing Day and January Sales: A Shoppers Guide
posts.seoDescription: A shoppers guide to Boxing Day and January sales, covering where the deepest discounts appear and how to avoid leftover low-quality stock.
posts.body:
The post-Christmas sales can be the best of the year, or a trap of leftover stock. A little care keeps you on the right side.

## What drops most
Winter clothing, bedding, gift sets and last-season electronics fall the most as stores clear space.

## Watch for low-quality stock
Some sale items are made specifically for the event. Check model numbers and reviews, not just the price.

## Use the January reset
New-year clearance on home and white goods often beats Black Friday for older models.

## Keep gift receipts
If you are buying gifts early for next year, confirm the return window still applies.

## Set a budget
Post-holiday fatigue makes overspending easy. Decide your total before you browse.

posts.title: How to Get the Best Deals on Flights and Hotels
posts.excerpt: Booking windows, flexible dates and member rates that cut travel costs.
posts.author: Biorals Team
posts.seoTitle: How to Get the Best Deals on Flights and Hotels
posts.seoDescription: Learn how flexible dates, booking windows and member rates can cut the cost of flights and hotels, plus how to spot genuine travel deals.
posts.body:
Travel deals reward flexibility and timing more than codes. A few strategies consistently lower the price.

## Be flexible on dates
Shifting by a day or two often changes a fare by a large margin. Fare calendars make this visible.

## Book in the right window
Domestic flights often price best a few weeks out, while long-haul and holiday travel reward earlier booking.

## Use member rates
Hotel chains and booking sites give signed-in members lower prices than public listings.

## Compare the full cost
Baggage, transfers and resort fees can erase a cheap headline fare. Compare the all-in total.

## Set price alerts
Track a route or hotel and book when the price dips to your target, rather than guessing.

posts.title: Membership vs Coupon: Is a Paid Subscription Worth It?
posts.excerpt: Run the break-even maths before you pay for a loyalty or delivery plan.
posts.author: Biorals Team
posts.seoTitle: Membership vs Coupon: Is a Paid Subscription Worth It?
posts.seoDescription: Work out whether a paid loyalty, delivery or warehouse membership beats using free coupons by running a simple break-even calculation.
posts.body:
Paid memberships can beat coupons, but only if you use them enough. The maths is simple once you know your habits.

## Count your orders
If a delivery membership saves per order, estimate how many orders you place a month and multiply.

## Add the perks
Free delivery, member prices and early access all count. Estimate a realistic value, not the best case.

## Find the break-even
Divide the annual fee by the per-order saving to see how many orders you need to break even.

## Compare with free codes
A free code or welcome offer may cover your occasional purchases without a commitment.

## Review yearly
Cancel if your usage drops. A membership you forget to use is a cost, not a saving.

posts.title: How to Use Competitor Price Matching to Save More
posts.excerpt: Make retailers honour a lower price elsewhere, without a code.
posts.author: Biorals Team
posts.seoTitle: How to Use Price Matching to Save More
posts.seoDescription: Learn how retailer price matching works, which stores offer it and how to claim a lower competitor price quickly and reliably at checkout.
posts.body:
Price matching lets you get a competitor's lower price from the store you prefer. It is often faster than hunting for a code.

## Know who offers it
Many electronics, home and department stores price match. Check the policy before you buy.

## Have proof ready
Keep a live link or screenshot of the identical item at the lower price, including size and colour.

## Match the right item
The competitor item must be identical and in stock. Bundles and marketplace sellers are often excluded.

## Do it before checkout
Some stores match at the point of sale, others refund the difference after. Ask which applies.

## Combine where allowed
If the policy allows, apply a code after the match for extra savings, but confirm the rules first.

posts.title: First-Order Discounts: The Complete New-Customer Guide
posts.excerpt: How to claim welcome offers without creating clutter or missing expiry.
posts.author: Biorals Team
posts.seoTitle: First-Order Discounts: New-Customer Deals Guide
posts.seoDescription: A complete guide to first-order and new-customer discounts: how to find them, when they apply and how to use them before they expire.
posts.body:
New-customer offers are among the largest discounts available, but they come with rules. Plan to use them well.

## Where to find them
Signup pop-ups, app installs and newsletter forms usually carry the best welcome codes.

## One per customer
Most are limited to one per person or household. Do not count on repeating them.

## Use on a meaningful basket
Apply the welcome code to a purchase you actually want, so the saving is real.

## Check the expiry
Welcome codes often expire within days. Note the date the moment you get it.

## Mind the minimum spend
Some first-order codes require a minimum basket. Make sure you were going to spend that anyway.

posts.title: How to Cancel Subscriptions and Avoid Renewal Jumps
posts.excerpt: Stop paying full price when a cheap first year quietly renews.
posts.author: Biorals Team
posts.seoTitle: Cancel Subscriptions: Avoid Renewal Price Jumps
posts.seoDescription: Learn how to track subscription renewals, cancel before a price jump and re-qualify for introductory offers without losing what you need.
posts.body:
Introductory prices are designed to renew higher. A little tracking keeps subscriptions cheap.

## Note every renewal date
List subscriptions with their renewal dates and prices so nothing renews by surprise.

## Cancel before the jump
Set a reminder a week before renewal. Many services let you cancel and keep access until the period ends.

## Re-qualify where allowed
Some services offer a returning-customer deal after a break. Check the terms before relying on it.

## Downgrade instead
A lower tier often covers what you actually use. Review usage before renewal.

## Use virtual cards
A virtual card with a set limit prevents surprise charges and makes cancelling cleaner.

posts.title: Gift Card Discounts: Where to Buy Them for Less
posts.excerpt: Pay less than face value on cards you will actually spend.
posts.author: Biorals Team
posts.seoTitle: Gift Card Discounts: Where to Buy Them for Less
posts.seoDescription: Find out where to buy discounted gift cards, how to check balances safely and how to combine them with coupons for extra savings.
posts.body:
Discounted gift cards are a quiet way to save on stores you already use. A few safeguards keep it safe.

## Buy below face value
Retailers and resellers sometimes sell cards at a discount. Combine with a store code for a double saving.

## Check the balance first
If buying a resold card, verify the balance immediately and keep the receipt.

## Watch expiry and fees
Some cards carry inactivity fees or expiry dates. Read the terms before you buy.

## Use soon
A gift card you forget is money lost. Buy for a planned purchase, not speculatively.

## Mind the cashback rule
Orders paid partly with gift cards may not earn cashback. Check the program terms.

posts.title: Back-to-School Shopping: Save on Tech, Clothes and Supplies
posts.excerpt: A term-start checklist that spreads cost without overspending.
posts.author: Biorals Team
posts.seoTitle: Back-to-School Shopping: Save on Tech and Supplies
posts.seoDescription: A back-to-school savings checklist covering laptops, clothing and stationery, plus student discounts and timing tips to cut term-start costs.
posts.body:
Term-start costs add up fast. A short plan keeps the total down.

## Buy tech with education pricing
Laptops and software often have education stores that beat public codes.

## Shop the sales calendar
Late summer sales and tax-free weekends (where offered) are ideal for clothing and supplies.

## Bulk buy basics
Stationery and socks are cheaper in multi-packs. Split with other families if packs are large.

## Reuse where sensible
Last year bags and PE kits often survive. Put the saving toward the items that matter.

## Use student status
Verify once and use student discounts on clothing, tech and food through the term.

posts.title: Amazon Prime Day: How to Get Real Savings
posts.excerpt: Which categories actually drop, and how to avoid the noise.
posts.author: Biorals Team
posts.seoTitle: Amazon Prime Day: How to Get Real Savings
posts.seoDescription: Learn which categories genuinely drop on Prime Day, how to track prices and how to avoid impulse buys during the two-day sales event.
posts.body:
Prime Day is loud, but not every deal is good. Focus on the categories that really drop.

## What genuinely discounts
Amazon devices, small electronics, headphones and home gadgets tend to fall the most.

## Check price history
Confirm the deal is below the usual price, not just below a raised list price.

## Prefer lightning deals you planned for
Use a wishlist so you only chase discounts on items you already wanted.

## Watch bundle pricing
Bundles can hide a higher unit price. Compare the item alone.

## Do not buy just because
A discount on something you do not need is not a saving. Stick to your list.

posts.title: How to Complain and Get a Refund: Your Consumer Rights
posts.excerpt: A calm, step-by-step way to resolve a bad purchase.
posts.author: Biorals Team
posts.seoTitle: How to Complain and Get a Refund: Consumer Rights
posts.seoDescription: A step-by-step guide to complaining about a purchase and getting a refund, covering your consumer rights, chargebacks and escalation routes.
posts.body:
When something goes wrong, a clear paper trail gets faster results than anger. Follow these steps.

## Know your rights
Most regions give a right to a refund, repair or replacement for faulty goods. Check the rules where you live.

## Contact the retailer first
Use written channels and state the order number, the problem and the outcome you want.

## Keep evidence
Save photos, messages and receipts. A concise summary with evidence is hard to ignore.

## Escalate if needed
If the retailer stalls, a card chargeback or a consumer body can help. Note the deadlines.

## Stay factual
Calm, specific complaints get resolved faster than emotional ones.

posts.title: The 30-Day Rule: How to Time Big Purchases
posts.excerpt: A simple waiting rule that stops impulse buys and catches real discounts.
posts.author: Biorals Team
posts.seoTitle: The 30-Day Rule: How to Time Big Purchases
posts.seoDescription: Use the 30-day rule to avoid impulse buys, track prices on big purchases and buy only when a discount is genuinely worth it.
posts.body:
Big purchases are where small decisions matter most. A waiting rule removes the pressure to buy on impulse.

## Write it down
When you feel the urge to buy, note the item and the date. Wait 30 days before deciding.

## Track the price meanwhile
A price tracker during the wait shows whether the price really moves or the discount is cosmetic.

## Decide with a clear head
After the wait, if you still want it and the price is right, buy with confidence.

## Let sales come to you
Waiting often lines up with a seasonal sale or a working code, so you rarely lose out.

## Break the rule rarely
Genuine limited-time clearance is the exception. Use the rule everywhere else.

pages.title: Money-Saving Tips: Cut the Cost of Everything
pages.seoTitle: Money-Saving Tips to Cut the Cost of Everything
pages.seoDescription: Practical money-saving tips that work with coupons: timing, cashback, price tracking and avoiding impulse buys on everyday spending.

Saving well is a set of habits, not a single coupon. These tips compound.

## Time your purchases
Buy out of season and around predictable sales. Our [saving guides](/guides/) show a month-by-month calendar.

## Stack legally
Use a code first, then loyalty points, then cashback. Respect each program rules to keep your savings.

## Track prices
A quick price check stops you paying a fake discount. Buy on a genuine dip, not a raised list price.

## Avoid impulse buys
The 30-day rule for big purchases rarely costs you a better price and often saves you from a mistake.

pages.title: Coupon Glossary: Key Terms Explained
pages.seoTitle: Coupon Glossary: Promo Code Terms Explained
pages.seoDescription: A plain-English coupon glossary covering promo code, voucher code, cashback, stacking, minimum spend, and other common shopping terms.
pages.body:
Shopping jargon can be confusing. Here are the terms you will see most.

## Promo code / voucher code
A code entered at checkout to reduce the price. Region names differ: the UK often says voucher code.

## Cashback
A share of your spend returned later through a cashback site, after the retailer confirms the order.

## Stacking
Combining more than one saving, such as a code plus loyalty points, where the store allows it.

## Minimum spend
The basket total you must reach for a code to apply.

## Price anchoring
Showing a high original price to make a sale price feel like a bargain.

Buy basics in multi-packs and time larger purchases for end-of-season sales.
